title: THE CURSE OF HOLLOW'S END
author: Adventure Designer
description: A Gothic horror adventure where you must lift the curse that plagues Hollow's End by confronting the vengeful spirit of the Widow and uncovering the dark secrets of the Hollow family.

alchemists-journal.name: Alchemist's Journal
alchemists-journal.description: Notes on the binding of the Widow.
alchemists-journal.text:
A torn, bloodstained page:

"The Widow is bound by silver chains and dark magic, but the binding is imperfect. It was never meant to last forever - only long enough for the guilty generation to die in peace.

To properly seal her spirit for eternity requires three components: silver forged specifically for binding (such as the Silver Key), her true name spoken with authority, and the ritual performed at the moment of greatest supernatural power (midnight on the anniversary of her binding).

Without all three components, the binding will be temporary at best. The Widow will eventually break free again, perhaps even more powerful than before."

diary.text:
"Day 12 of captivity: The Widow's wail is stronger tonight. It pierces the walls, pierces my ears, pierces my very mind. I cannot sleep.

Day 13: Sleep deprivation is taking its toll. I hear things that aren't there. See shadows that move when I'm not looking. The food is almost gone.

Day 14: They're at the door. I can hear them scratching, moaning, calling my name in voices of the dead. I've barricaded myself in, but I know it won't hold forever. If anyone finds this - tell my family I love them. Tell them I -"

The entry ends there, unfinished. The diary tells you nothing useful, only how deadly the curse is.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Background

Two hundred and forty-two years ago, on what should have been the happiest day of her life, Eliza Hollow was betrayed by her own family. Her father, Mordecai Hollow, murdered her beloved Thomas Ashford during their wedding ceremony and used forbidden necromancy to bind Eliza's spirit in eternal torment.

For generations, the Hollow family lived in fear as the curse grew stronger. Now the binding has finally broken, and the Widow has risen with an army of undead. The village of Hollow's End stands on the brink of destruction.

You are an adventurer who has answered Mayor Aldric Hollow's desperate call for help. Can you discover the Widow's true name, obtain the silver key, and bind her spirit before midnight strikes? The fate of Hollow's End rests in your hands.

You stand at the entrance to Hollow's End as twilight deepens into true night, watching the last vestiges of daylight abandon this forsaken place to whatever horrors the darkness will bring. The transition from day to night feels faster here, more absolute, as if the sun itself is fleeing from what it knows lurks in the shadows.

A weathered wooden sign marks the village boundary. The paint is peeling, the wood rotting from years of neglect, but you can still make out the faded letters: "HOLLOW'S END — POP. 247"

Someone has scratched through the number with what looks disturbingly like dried blood, writing below: "232 and falling."

The wind carries with it the scent of decay and turned earth. In the distance, you hear something that might be moaning... or might just be the wind itself moving through the abandoned buildings. It's impossible to tell, and somehow that uncertainty is worse than knowing.

Three paths lie before you, each leading into the gathering gloom:

To the left: A ramshackle tavern hunches against the growing darkness like a wounded animal seeking shelter. A swinging sign reads "The Weeping Willow" in faded gold letters that catch the last rays of dying light. Warm yellow light flickers in the windows—an inviting beacon in this dead village. Through the dusty glass, you can see shadows moving inside. Perhaps someone there has information about the curse. Perhaps they have ale to steady your nerves for what's to come. Or perhaps something darker waits behind that welcoming facade.

Straight ahead: The cemetery gates stand twisted and torn open, as if something of immense strength had burst through from the inside out. The iron bars are bent outward at impossible angles, and deep gouges score the metal—claw marks from something that should not exist. Even from here, you can see fresh graves lying exposed, their earth disturbed, their wooden markers toppled, their occupants missing. The very heart of the curse, no doubt, and perhaps the quickest way to confront whatever evil plagues this place. But also the most dangerous.

To the right: The Mayor's manor dominates the village square—a grand three-story building that must have been magnificent once but now looks haunted even before true darkness falls. Its windows are dark except for a few where candlelight flickers weakly, as if afraid to shine too brightly. You can see figures moving behind curtains, hurried and furtive. This is where Mayor Aldric Hollow lives, the man who sent the desperate call for help that brought you here. He will have information, resources, and perhaps the key to understanding the curse that stems from his own family's sins.

Each path offers different opportunities and different dangers. The choice is yours, but choose wisely—your first decision may determine whether you live or die in the hours ahead.

{{opt:to-45}}
{{opt:to-127}}
{{opt:to-234}}

You drink the mysterious liquid without hesitation, hoping it might be some sort of healing potion or protective elixir. The moment the vile concoction touches your lips, you realize your terrible mistake.

The taste is indescribable—bitter as poison, thick as mud, with an underlying sweetness that makes your stomach revolt. Your vision blurs immediately, the room spinning sickeningly around you as if reality itself is becoming unmoored. Your limbs grow heavy as lead, refusing to respond to your desperate commands. The liquid burns down your throat like liquid fire, and you can feel it spreading through your body like corruption through healthy flesh.

Your knees buckle. You try to cry out but your tongue has gone numb. Colors bleed together, sounds become distorted, and you feel yourself falling, falling, falling...

When your vision finally clears and the world stops spinning, you find yourself on your hands and knees, gasping for breath. Your body feels weaker, your mind sluggish, your reflexes dulled. Whatever that substance was, it was certainly not meant for consumption—at least not by the living.

Reduce your SKILL by 2 and your STAMINA by 4.

Your head pounds with agony as you struggle to remain conscious. You've survived the poisoning, but you're significantly weakened. Every movement requires conscious effort, and you can feel the toxin still coursing through your veins, making your muscles ache and your thoughts   
fuzzy.

Shaken and diminished, you force yourself to your feet and continue.

{{opt:to-78}}

The cultist falls with a final gurgling breath, his hooded face hitting the stone floor with a wet thump. His eyes glaze over as whatever dark light animated them fades into nothingness. For a moment, his body twitches as if something is trying to escape it, then lies still.

You search his corpse carefully, trying not to think about the still-warm blood soaking into your hands. Hidden in the folds of his dark robes, you find a brass key with strange symbols etched into its surface—symbols that seem to writhe and shift when you're not looking directly at them. The metal is cold to the touch, unnaturally cold, as if it's been lying in ice rather than against warm flesh.

There's also a crumpled note clutched in his other hand, written in a hasty, almost panicked scrawl. The ink is fresh, the paper trembling slightly in your grip as if it too carries some residual dark energy:

"The Wight awakens at midnight in the eastern chamber. Feed it the girl's blood to complete the ritual. The Widow will rise at her full power, and her vengeance will be complete. Hollow's End will fall, and we shall be rewarded beyond measure. Our master's will be done."

The note is unsigned, but the implications are chilling. Somewhere in these catacombs or in the village above, cultists are planning to sacrifice an innocent girl to further empower the curse. A Wight awaits. And midnight is the deadline.

Add the BRASS KEY to your Adventure Sheet.

{{opt:to-180}}

sections.title: INSTANT DEATH!
sections.text:
INSTANT DEATH!

The floor collapses beneath you without the slightest warning. One moment you're standing on what appears to be solid stone, the next you're plummeting into darkness as ancient wood and rotted supports finally succumb to time and weight.

Your arms flail uselessly, fingers grasping at empty air. A scream tears from your throat, echoing in the void as you fall into the blackness below.

Then you see them—rusted iron spikes rising from the pit floor like the teeth of some monstrous beast, dozens of them, their points dulled by time but still more than sharp enough to pierce flesh and bone.

You land with a sickening crunch. The spikes punch through your armor, through flesh and muscle and bone, pinning you like an insect in a collector's case. Pain explodes through your body—white-hot agony that makes thought impossible.

Your vision darkens at the edges. The pain becomes distant. You can hear your heartbeat slowing... slowing... stopping...

Your adventure ends here, impaled in a forgotten trap. Your body will never be found. The curse continues, and Hollow's End remains doomed.

THE END

The door opens with a shriek of tortured metal that echoes through the chamber like the cry of a damned soul. The sound sets your teeth on edge and sends shivers racing down your spine. Rust rains down from the hinges as they move for the first time in decades—perhaps centuries.

Inside, the chamber is dominated by a massive stone sarcophagus covered in warning runes carved deep into the ancient stone. Heavy iron chains, now rusted through, lie scattered on the floor, their links broken and useless.

You approach cautiously, every instinct screaming at you to turn back. But you came here for answers.

As your shadow falls across the sarcophagus, the massive stone lid suddenly explodes outward with tremendous force!

Chunks of ancient stone fly past your head. Through the debris and dust, you see a figure rising from within—a Cursed Wight, its flesh dried and mummified but animated by dark magic. Its eyes burn with unholy red fire. This is not a mindless zombie—this is an undead creature of immense power and malevolent cunning.

The Wight opens its desiccated mouth in a soundless scream of eternal rage and lunges forward!

Special Ability - Life Drain: Each time this creature wounds you, it permanently reduces your maximum STAMINA by 1. This damage cannot be healed by any means—your life essence is literally being drained away.

combat.victoryText: The creature collapses with a final, soundless scream, its mummified form crumbling to dust and ancient bones. As the dark magic dissipates, you can breathe easier.  to search the chamber for treasures and information

sections.text:
Your survival instincts scream at you to hide, and you quickly duck into a shadowed alcove, pressing yourself flat against the cold stone wall and trying to quiet your breathing. Your heart hammers in your chest so loudly you're certain it will give you away.

The darkness embraces you like a cold shroud as you watch and wait.

Moments later, two robed cultists pass by your hiding spot. They're discussing something in low, urgent tones:

"The ritual proceeds according to plan," one says. "By midnight tonight, the Widow will have her sacrifice. Her chains will be broken completely, and her full power will be unleashed."

"The master grows impatient," the other responds nervously. "We must not fail. If the binding is not broken completely by midnight..." "It will be broken," the first interrupts. "We have the girl. We have the ritual components. Nothing can stop us now." Their voices fade as they move past.

{{roll}}

success.text: They do not sense your presence.

failure.text: You have been detected!

outcomes.text: You catch a narrow ledge and survive the fall.
Your fall ends in disaster. Test your Luck to catch a ledge.

success.text: At the last instant you snatch a ledge and break your fall, badly hurt.

failure.text: You hit the stone floor and the darkness takes you!

sections.text:
Your careful searching reveals a hidden cache behind a loose stone! Someone has stashed valuable items here. Inside, wrapped in oil cloth, you find:

30 Gold Pieces

2 Healing Potions (each restores 4 STAMINA)

A rusty iron key

Add these items to your Adventure Sheet.

Fortune smiles upon you. These items could prove invaluable in the challenges ahead.

{{opt:to-111}}

sections.title: The Ghost's wail pierces your skull like a spike of ice!

success.text: The wail fades; your ears ring but you are intact.

failure.text: The wail tears at your very essence.

sections.text:
You manage to sneak past the undead guardians successfully, moving with careful, silent steps. Your heart pounds like a war drum, but your breathing remains controlled.

The guardians pass within inches of where you hide, pressed against the cold stone wall. You can smell them—the dry, dusty scent of ancient bones, or the cold, ozone-tinged aroma of spectral energy.

They don't detect your presence. Once their footsteps fade, you dare to breathe normally again. Relief washes over you. Beyond the guardians, the passage splits into three separate ways, each leading into darkness.

{{opt:to-111}}

The bartender's eyes go completely black like pools of ink, spreading from pupil to sclera in an unnatural wave. His unnaturally wide smile drops, replaced by a snarl that reveals teeth far too sharp to be human.

"You shouldn't have come here," he says, but the voice is wrong—layered, as if multiple throats speak at once. His form begins to ripple like water, skin flowing and shifting as his true nature reveals itself.

This is no human bartender. It's something far worse—a shapeshifter, a doppelganger, a creature that wears human faces like masks and disposes of them just as easily.

{{opt:to-78}}

You drink the healing potion quickly, feeling its magic course through your body like liquid warmth spreading through your veins. The sensation is pleasant, almost euphoric—the polar opposite of the cold darkness that seems to permeate this cursed place.

The wounds on your body close before your eyes, flesh knitting together, blood ceasing to flow. Bruises fade from purple and black to yellow to healthy flesh tones in seconds. The exhaustion that had been weighing on your limbs like lead chains lifts away, replaced by renewed vigor and strength.

Restore 4 STAMINA points (maximum of your Initial STAMINA).

You take a deep breath, flex your fingers, roll your shoulders. The potion has done its work well. You feel refreshed, rejuvenated, ready to face whatever horrors await in the darkness ahead.

{{opt:to-234}}

options.label: Unlock the door with the Brass Key

sections.text:
You find a hidden compartment cunningly concealed within the altar's base, so well-crafted that only the most thorough search would reveal it. Your fingers trace the edges of what appears to be solid stone until you find the tiny catch that releases the hidden panel.

Inside, protected by wax sealing and wrapped in ancient silk that crumbles at your touch, lies a scroll written in elegant but faded script. The parchment is old—centuries old—but the ink has been preserved by the wax and silk wrapping. Your hands tremble slightly as you unroll it and read the words that could change everything:

"Let it be known to any who seek to bind the vengeful spirit: The Widow's true name, hidden from all but those who dare to search the darkest places, is ELIZA HOLLOW. Speak this name with authority and proper binding, and her power may be contained. But beware—to speak her name is to draw her attention. Be certain you are prepared to face her wrath before you invoke it."

This is crucial information! The Widow's true name is one of the three critical items needed for victory. Without it, you cannot properly bind her spirit. Add "Widow's True Name: ELIZA HOLLOW" to your Adventure Sheet.

You carefully memorize the name, speaking it silently to yourself several times to ensure it's burned into your memory: Eliza Hollow. Eliza Hollow. ELIZA HOLLOW.

{{opt:to-245}}

A Zombie lurches from the shadows without warning, its rotting hand clamping around your ankle with surprising strength! The flesh is cold and slimy, already beginning to slough off the bone, but the grip is like iron. You can feel the unnatural power animating this corpse—it's far stronger than any dead thing has a right to be.

The Zombie's face is a nightmare of decay—skin hanging in strips, one eye missing from its socket, jaw hanging askew where the tendons have rotted through. Yet it moves with terrible purpose, dragging itself toward you with single-minded hunger.

The stench is overwhelming—rot and death and something worse, something unnatural. Your stomach heaves, but there's no time for weakness. This creature means to drag you down, to tear you apart with teeth and broken fingernails, to add you to the army of the undead.

There's no time to flee, no room to maneuver. You must fight!

Special Rule: You cannot flee from this combat once it begins. The Zombie has hold of your ankle and won't release until one of you is destroyed. Fight for your life!

You hold up the Cult Medallion boldly, stepping into the chamber with false confidence. The medallion is cold against your palm, its weight somehow heavier than mere metal should be. The symbols etched into its surface seem to pulse with a faint, sickly light.

"Brothers," you announce in a steady voice, trying to sound like you belong here, like you've been part of this dark fellowship for years rather than minutes. "I've come from the eastern catacombs with news from our dark master."

The cultists turn toward you as one, their hooded faces impossible to read in the flickering candlelight. For a terrible moment—a moment that seems to stretch into eternity—you think they see through your deception. You imagine them drawing hidden daggers, imagine them crying out in alarm, imagine the ritual being interrupted not to save the girl but to sacrifice you instead.

Then the nearest cultist nods slowly, the movement almost reverent.

"Welcome, brother," he intones in a voice thick with dark fervor. "Your timing is fortuitous. The ritual proceeds as planned. The Widow will rise at the stroke of midnight, and her vengeance will finally be complete. Hollow's End will become the first of many—a spreading darkness that will consume the world of the living."

The other cultists murmur agreement, their attention returning to their dark work. You've been accepted, at least for now. Moving carefully, maintaining your disguise, you edge closer to the ritual circle, listening to every word of their plans.

The information you overhear could mean the difference between saving this village and watching it fall to eternal darkness. {{opt:to-245}}

The passage ahead narrows dramatically, the walls pressing in from both sides until you can barely fit through. The ceiling lowers as well, forcing you to hunch forward, then to crouch, then finally to crawl on hands and knees. The air grows thick and stale, heavy with the weight of earth and stone pressing down from above.

Claustrophobia claws at your mind. What if you get stuck? What if the walls close in further? What if the ceiling collapses? You can feel the weight of the entire cemetery, perhaps the entire village, pressing down on this fragile tunnel.

Your armor scrapes against the stone walls with sounds that seem impossibly loud in the confined space. Each inch forward requires effort, your shoulders barely fitting through gaps that seem to shrink with every passing moment.

{{roll}}

success.text: You squeeze through the tight space.

failure.text: You become stuck and scrape yourself free.

sections.text:
A spectral hand, translucent and glowing with unnatural blue light, passes directly through your chest!

The sensation is beyond description—icy cold that penetrates to your very core, as if someone has wrapped frozen fingers around your heart and squeezed. You stagger back, gasping, unable to breathe, unable to think, unable to do anything but experience the violation of having something from beyond death reach inside your living body.

The cold spreads from your chest outward, flowing through your veins like ice water, making your fingers numb, your toes numb, your face numb. For a terrible moment, you think you're going to die—that your heart will simply stop, frozen by this supernatural touch.

Then the hand withdraws, pulling back through your chest as if your flesh and bone were nothing but mist. The immediate cold fades, but something worse remains—a lingering chill in your core, a weakness in your limbs, a fog in your mind that wasn't there before.

The ghostly attack has taken its toll on your very essence, draining away part of what makes you alive, part of what makes you strong. Permanently lose 3 STAMINA and 1 SKILL.

These attributes are reduced from both your current AND maximum scores. Mark this carefully on your Adventure Sheet. Even if you find healing, even if you rest, this damage cannot be undone. The ghost has stolen part of your life force, and it's gone forever.

Shaken to your core, literally and figuratively, you force yourself to continue forward, feeling diminished in ways you can't quite articulate. {{opt:to-301}}

You find the real bartender in the cellar, bound with thick ropes and gagged with a cloth that's been tied so tight it's cut into the corners of his mouth. His eyes are wide with terror, rimmed red from crying or lack of sleep or both. When he sees you descending the stairs—a living, breathing human being rather than the monster that's been wearing his face—relief floods his features so completely that tears begin streaming down his cheeks.

You quickly cut him free with your blade. His hands are numb from the tight bonds, and he gasps as circulation returns, painful but necessary. He tears the gag from his mouth, spitting and coughing.

"Thank the gods! Thank every god that ever was!" His voice is hoarse from disuse and dehydration. "That... that thing replaced me two nights ago. I've been trapped down here, listening to it upstairs, serving customers, pretending to be me. It's been watching the mayor's house, reporting to someone in the catacombs. I heard it talking to... to things that shouldn't exist."

He staggers to his feet on unsteady legs, then reaches into a hidden alcove you hadn't noticed. "Take this—it's all I have saved. You'll need it more than me if you're going to face what's out there."

Inside a small chest, you find:

50 Gold Pieces

1 Healing Potion (restores 4 STAMINA)

Add these to your Adventure Sheet.   
"The mayor," the bartender continues, gripping your arm with surprising strength despite his ordeal. "Mayor Hollow knows more about all this. It's connected to his family's past, to something terrible that happened generations ago. And there are cultists—robed figures moving through the village after dark, heading to catacombs beneath the cemetery."

He shudders, wrapping his arms around himself. "Please. Whatever you're here to do, do it quickly. Before we all end up like those poor souls in the graveyard—dead but not resting."

{{opt:to-234}}
{{opt:to-127}}

The ancient bridge before you is a death trap waiting to spring. The wood is rotten and treacherous, its planks slick with moss and moisture that never fully dries in this lightless place. The ropes that once held it secure have frayed to the point where individual fibers are visible, ready to snap at the slightest stress.

Below, you can't see the bottom—just darkness that seems to go down forever, with the faint sound of water running far, far below. How far would you fall? Twenty feet? Fifty? A hundred? And what waits at the bottom—water to break your fall, or rocks to break your body?

The bridge groans ominously as you step onto it, the sound like an old man crying out in pain. Each plank bends under your weight, and you can feel the structure shifting, settling, threatening to collapse entirely.

{{roll}}

success.text: The bridge holds.

failure.text: The bridge collapses!

sections.text:
You sit down at a table and consume one of your precious Provisions, taking the time to actually taste the food and rest your weary body. The simple act of eating something that isn't soaked in blood or touched by death feels almost sacred in this place of horror.

The food is plain—dried meat, hard bread, a bit of cheese that's starting to go soft—but it tastes like the finest feast. Your body craves the sustenance, and as you eat, you can feel strength returning to your limbs, clarity returning to your thoughts.

Restore 4 STAMINA (maximum of your Initial STAMINA).

Cross off one Provision from your Adventure Sheet.

You take a moment to catch your breath, to let your muscles relax, to remind yourself why you're doing this—to save innocent people from a fate worse than death. The brief rest fortifies not just your body but your resolve.

When you finish eating, you wipe your mouth, stretch your aching muscles, and prepare to continue your quest. {{opt:to-127}}

success.text: You resist the worst of the paralysis. Your arm tingles but still works.

failure.text: The paralysis takes hold; your arm turns slow and weak.

sections.text:
Your keen eyes spot something the casual observer would miss—a narrow opening in the wall, so cunningly concealed that it appears to be nothing more than a natural crack in the stone. But when you press against it, a section of wall swings inward, revealing a secret passage!

The passage is narrow and dark, with walls that show tool marks from the original excavation. This isn't a natural formation—someone carved this tunnel deliberately, perhaps as an escape route, perhaps to bypass a dangerous section of the catacombs.

The air that flows from the passage is fresher than the stale, death-tinged atmosphere of the main catacombs. This route must connect to a different section, one that's less traveled by the undead.

Add 1 LUCK for this fortunate discovery. Sometimes the gods of fortune smile upon the brave.

You slip into the secret passage, leaving the flooded section behind. The passage winds through the earth, bypassing who knows what dangers, and eventually opens into a different corridor entirely.

{{opt:to-155}}

The Mayor's expression shifts from desperate hope to suspicion, his eyes narrowing as he studies you more carefully. His hand moves slowly toward something hidden beneath his desk—a weapon? An alarm bell?

"How do I know you're not one of them?" he asks, voice tight with fear and paranoia. "How do I know you're not a cultist, or worse—some thrall of the Widow herself, sent to finish what my ancestors started?"

His question isn't unreasonable. In a village besieged by undead and dark cultists, trust is a luxury no one can afford.

Do you have the MAYOR'S LEDGER—the book you found hidden in the tavern, the one that details payments to the "Hollow Faith" cult and contains incriminating information about his family?

If you have the MAYOR'S LEDGER: You produce the ledger, laying it on his desk. His face goes white as he recognizes it. "Gods above... where did you find this? Father hid this years ago. If you have this, you must have faced real dangers already." He slumps back in his chair, the fight draining out of him. "Forgive me. I had to be certain. Let me help you properly." {{opt:to-234}}

If you don't have the ledger: The Mayor's suspicion hardens into conviction. "Get out!" he shouts, his voice cracking with fear and anger. "Get out of my house! I won't let the cult trick me into helping them!" He draws a pistol from beneath his desk, his hand shaking but his aim steady enough. "LEAVE! NOW!"

You have no choice but to retreat. You've lost a valuable ally, and worse—you can no longer obtain the SILVER KEY that Mayor Hollow possesses, one of the three critical items needed to bind the Widow.

Without the Silver Key, true victory is now impossible.

{{opt:to-127}}

You try reasoning with the Widow, stepping forward with your hands raised in a gesture of peace. Perhaps there's some way to reach the human being she once was, some spark of Eliza Hollow that remains beneath the rage and darkness.

"Eliza," you begin, using her true name carefully. "What was done to you was terrible. Unforgivable. But this—raising the dead, terrorizing the innocent—this isn't justice. This is—"

"SILENCE!"

Her scream is so loud, so filled with rage and anguish, that it physically pushes you backward. The temperature in the room plummets. The walls themselves seem to shake with the force of her fury.

"You DARE speak to me of justice? You, who live and breathe and walk in sunlight while I rotted in chains for TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO YEARS? You know NOTHING of suffering! NOTHING of injustice! I will teach you! I will teach ALL the living what I endured!"

Her form expands, growing larger, more terrible. Her face twists into something barely human. And from the shadows around her, three dark shapes detach and rush toward you—Shadows, creatures of pure darkness and hatred, manifestations of the Widow's rage given semi-solid form.

You must fight all three!

Special Ability - Strength Drain: Each time a Shadow successfully wounds you, it permanently reduces your SKILL by 1. The Shadows literally drain your combat ability, making each subsequent round harder.

Fight the Shadows one at a time in the order listed.

You drink the mysterious potion without hesitation, tipping the vial back and letting the thick liquid flow down your throat. For a moment, nothing happens. Then you feel it—warmth spreading through your body, but it's different from a healing potion. This is something else entirely.

{{roll}}

success.text: The potion is a powerful healing draft!

failure.text: The potion was poisoned!

sections.text:
You smash through the door with a powerful kick, putting all your strength and desperation into the blow. The wood splinters around the lock, ancient boards cracking and giving way under the assault. The door flies inward, slamming against the stone wall with a crash that echoes through the chamber.

Inside, chained to a stone pillar in the center of the room, you find her—Lydia, the Mayor's daughter. She's pale, so pale she looks almost ghostly in the flickering torchlight. Her dress is torn and dirty, her hair matted, her wrists raw and bleeding where the iron manacles have cut into her flesh.

But she's alive.

Her eyes fly open at the sound of your entrance, wide with terror until she sees you're not one of her captors. Then hope—desperate, almost painful hope—floods her face.

"Please," she whispers, her voice hoarse from disuse or screaming or both. "Please help me. They're going to... the ritual... tonight at the manor. They're going to sacrifice me at midnight to complete the Widow's resurrection. I heard them talking. If they succeed, she'll have enough power to spread the curse beyond Hollow's End, to consume entire regions."

You rush forward, examining her chains. They're secured with a heavy iron lock, but your weapons make short work of it. The chains fall away with a clatter, and Lydia nearly collapses. You catch her, steadying her until she can stand on her own.

"Thank you," she sobs, clinging to you for a moment. "Thank you. I have to get back to my father. He must be terrified." You help her toward the exit, supporting her weight as she stumbles on legs that haven't walked in days.

{{opt:to-245}}

sections.title: DEAD END.
sections.text:
DEAD END.

The passage ahead has collapsed completely, tons of earth and stone blocking any forward progress. The ceiling shows ominous cracks, suggesting that this cave-in happened recently and that more could follow. Dust still hangs in the air, and small pebbles occasionally fall from above, pattering down like deadly rain.

You can't proceed this way. Attempting to dig through would take days, even if you had the tools, and would likely bring the entire ceiling down on your head. The unstable nature of the collapse means that even standing here is dangerous.

You have no choice but to turn back and find another route. The frustration of hitting a dead end weighs on you—time is precious, and every minute wasted is a minute closer to midnight.

Lose 1 STAMINA from the physical effort of your attempted approach and the stress of the setback.

Turn back and choose a different path. {{opt:to-111}}

options.label: Carry the Silver Key to the final confrontation
Without the Silver Key, press on regardless
Keep searching for the Silver Key

sections.text:
A Skeleton Warrior blocks your path, its bones held together by dark magic and rusty wire. Unlike the shambling zombies or mindless skeletons you've faced before, this one moves with purpose and intelligence. It wears the remnants of ancient armor and grips a corroded but still-deadly sword in its bony hands.

As you approach, its skull turns toward you, empty eye sockets somehow still conveying malevolence. The jaw opens and closes in a parody of speech, though no sound emerges—just the click-clack of bone on bone.

It assumes a combat stance, sword raised, ready to defend this passage to the death—or whatever passes for death when you're already dead.

Special Weakness: If you're wielding a mace or club (crushing weapons), you deal 3 damage instead of the normal 2. Bones shatter more easily under blunt force trauma than they break from cuts.

Fight the Skeleton Warrior!

You climb the stone stairs carefully, one hand on the wall for balance, the other on your weapon. The stairs are worn smooth by centuries of feet, creating shallow depressions in the center of each step. How many people have climbed these stairs over the years? How many descended them never to return?

The stairs spiral upward through the earth, lit occasionally by guttering torches that cast dancing shadows on the walls. The air grows slightly less oppressive as you climb—not fresh exactly, but less heavy with the stench of death and decay.

Finally, you emerge into what appears to be the ground floor of the Hollow manor, or perhaps a level just below it. You find yourself in a grand hallway, its walls lined with portraits in ornate frames. But something is wrong with the portraits—every single face has been scratched out, gouged away as if by furious claws. The damage is recent too; you can see pale wood where the painted canvas has been torn.

Who destroyed these portraits? The Widow herself, in a rage against the Hollow family? Cultists, trying to erase evidence of their identities? Or the portraits' own subjects, unable to bear looking at themselves anymore?

The hallway stretches in both directions, doors visible at intervals along its length. Somewhere in this manor, the Widow waits. Somewhere here, the final confrontation approaches.

{{opt:to-301}}

A cultist materializes from the shadows without warning, his approach so silent you don't detect him until he's almost upon you. His face is hidden beneath a deep hood, but his eyes gleam with fanatical fervor in the darkness—the eyes of a true believer, someone who has surrendered all reason and mercy to a dark cause.

He spots you immediately, and his hand flies to the ceremonial dagger at his belt.

"Intruder!" he hisses, his voice dripping with hatred. "You dare defile our sacred space! The Widow will feast on your soul!"   
He attacks without hesitation, without any attempt at negotiation or flight. Cultists like this are perhaps more dangerous than the undead—they have intelligence, skill, and the willingness to die for their cause.

Fight for your life!

options.label: Use the Mayor's Ledger to read the symbols

sections.text:
The floor ahead looks solid enough, but your instincts—honed by years of adventure and countless brushes with death—scream warning. Something about the stones ahead looks wrong. The mortar between them is a slightly different color. The stones themselves sit at a subtly different height. It's a trap.

{{roll}}

success.text: You spot the pressure plate and step around it.

failure.text: Darts shoot from the walls!

options.label: Drink the vial now (+1 SKILL permanently, -1 LUCK)
Take the vial with you to drink later
Leave the vial behind and continue

sections.text:
A translucent figure materializes before you, blocking your path completely. The Phantom Servant wears the tattered remains of what was once fine livery—the uniform of a servant in the Hollow household, now little more than ethereal rags hanging from its ghostly form.

Its face is twisted in eternal anguish, mouth open in a silent scream that you can somehow still hear in your mind. This was once a person— someone who served the Hollow family, someone who died (or was killed) and whose spirit was bound to serve even in death.

The ghost doesn't attack out of malice but out of compulsion. It's following orders given long ago: "Let no one pass." It doesn't matter that those who gave the orders are long dead, that the entity it serves is now an evil thing. The Phantom Servant knows only duty, and it will fight to the end to fulfill it.

Special Ability - Incorporeal: As a ghostly entity, it exists partially outside normal reality. Normal weapons deal only 1 damage instead of the usual 2 when they strike it. Magical weapons or silver weapons deal normal damage.

Fight the Phantom Servant!

You manage to overhear fragments of conversation between cultists before they move out of earshot:

"...Widow needs the girl's blood for the final phase..."

"...the old binding must be destroyed completely..."

"...midnight bell at the manor will signal the ritual's beginning..."

"...silver chains will finally break..."

"...true name must never be spoken by the living..."

The information comes in disjointed pieces, but together they paint a terrifying picture. The cultists plan to sacrifice Mayor Aldric's daughter Lydia. They're working to destroy whatever remains of the original binding that held the Widow's power in check. The ritual will take place at midnight in the Hollow manor. And the Widow's true name is something they desperately want to keep secret.

Knowledge is power, and you've just gained valuable intelligence that could help you stop the ritual before it's too late. {{opt:to-180}}

Lydia looks up at you with gratitude and tears streaming down her face. "Thank you," she whispers, her voice trembling. "Thank you for saving me. I thought I was going to die down here, that my last moments would be watching those monsters drink my blood for their dark ritual."

She's weak from her ordeal—days without food, little water, and the constant terror of knowing what awaited her at midnight. You help her to her feet, supporting her weight as she stumbles on unsteady legs.

"I need to get back to my father," she says urgently. "He must be out of his mind with worry. And you... you need to stop them. The cult is planning something terrible. They talked about it constantly, thinking I couldn't understand their hints and coded language. But I figured it out."

You escort Lydia through the catacombs, retracing your steps toward the surface. The journey is slower with her injured and exhausted, but eventually you emerge into the village above. The moon hangs heavy and full in the sky—how many hours until midnight?

You deliver Lydia safely to her father's house. Mayor Aldric weeps when he sees his daughter alive, crushing her in an embrace that makes her wince but also smile through her tears.

"You saved her," he says to you, his voice thick with emotion. "You actually saved her. I... I don't have words. Thank you doesn't seem like enough." True to his promise, the Mayor takes you to his hidden vault and retrieves an ornate silver key, its surface inscribed with binding runes.

"This was used by my grandfather to help imprison the Widow originally," he explains. "Without it, you cannot bind her spirit again. Use it well. End this curse forever."

You can now obtain the SILVER KEY! Add it to your Adventure Sheet.

This is one of the three critical items needed for victory.   
{{opt:to-234}} (the Mayor will help you further if you wish to consult with him).

sections.title: INSTANT DEATH!
sections.text:
INSTANT DEATH!

Without warning, a spectral blade materializes from thin air and plunges directly through your chest! The blade is transparent, ghostly, but the pain it causes is horrifyingly real. You look down in shock to see the ethereal weapon protruding from your chest, right where your heart should be.

Cold spreads from the wound—not the cold of ice, but the cold of the grave, of death itself. You try to cry out, but your lungs won't work. You try to pull the blade free, but your hands pass through it without finding purchase.

You fall to your knees, then to your side, your vision already darkening. The last thing you hear is laughter—the Widow's laughter, echoing from everywhere and nowhere, filled with cruel satisfaction.

"Another fool," her voice whispers in your dying ears. "Another victim. Join my army, little hero. Serve me in death as you failed to stop me in life."

Your adventure ends here, killed by the Widow's spectral power before you could even face her directly. Your body will rise as one of her undead servants, forever bound to serve the very evil you came to destroy.

THE END

You find an old journal, its pages yellowed and brittle but still legible. The handwriting is shaky, written by someone under extreme stress:

"The Hollow family bound the Widow with forbidden magic and silver chains. But the binding was never meant to be permanent—just long enough for my grandfather's generation to die in peace, leaving the problem for future generations.

The binding weakens with each generation that passes. Soon, perhaps in my children's time or their children's time, it will fail completely.

The only way to renew it is with the Widow's true name and silver forged specifically for binding spirits. The old silver key still exists, hidden in our family vault. But the true name... that knowledge was supposed to die with the original conspirators. Without both, the Widow cannot be properly bound again.

May God forgive us for what we did. May our descendants find the strength to right our wrongs."

The entry is unsigned and undated, but it provides crucial information about how the original binding worked and what's needed to renew it. Add this knowledge to your notes.

{{opt:to-355}}

The ceiling above you suddenly gives way without warning! Centuries of moisture and slow decay finally claim victory, and tons of earth and stone come crashing down.

{{roll}}

outcomes.text: You are caught by the edge of the collapse.

sections.text:
You search the corpse carefully, trying not to think too much about the gray flesh and the faint smell of decay. Among the dead cultist's belongings, you find a torn map showing a secret entrance to the manor—a tunnel that bypasses the main gates and most of the ground floor defenses.

This could prove invaluable! With this map, you can enter the manor undetected, potentially avoiding guards, traps, or other hazards that the main entrance might hold.

Add 1 LUCK for this fortunate discovery. Sometimes, fate smiles on the brave.   
Add the MAP to your Adventure Sheet.

You carefully fold the map and tuck it into your pack, then continue your exploration of this death-filled place.

{{opt:to-127}}

You discover a hidden laboratory, its door concealed behind a false wall that you only found through careful searching and no small amount of luck. Inside, the air smells of chemicals and dust, of old magic and forgotten experiments.

The laboratory is in disarray, as if someone left in a hurry and never returned. Glass vials lie shattered on the floor, their contents long since evaporated. Bookshelves have toppled, spilling their contents across the ground. Strange apparatus—alembics, retorts, devices whose purposes you can't even guess—lie broken and forgotten.

But on a desk in the corner, miraculously untouched by the chaos, sits a leather-bound journal. You pick it up carefully, blow the dust from its cover, and read the title embossed in fading gold letters:

"The Alchemist's Journal: Notes on Spectral Binding and the Hollow Family Curse"

Your heart races. This could be exactly what you need!

Add the ALCHEMIST'S JOURNAL to your Adventure Sheet.

This journal contains crucial information about how to defeat the Widow, including details about her true name, the binding ritual, and the items required to seal her spirit permanently. It's one of the most valuable items you could find.

{{opt:to-355}}

You attempt to pick the lock on the chest, using whatever tools you have at hand—a dagger tip, a piece of wire, your own fingernails if necessary. The lock is old and corroded, which works in your favor—the mechanism is stiff but also degraded.

Do you have THIEVES' TOOLS or specific lockpicking equipment?

If yes: The lock opens smoothly under your skilled manipulation.

If no: You'll have to try forcing it. {{roll}}

If you successfully opened the chest:

Inside, carefully wrapped in oil cloth to protect against moisture, you find:

40 Gold Pieces

CLOAK OF PROTECTION - A fine garment woven with subtle protective enchantments. When worn, it adds +1 to your Armor Class and +1 to all saving throws against magical effects. The cloak is dark blue, almost black, and surprisingly light despite its apparent thickness.

Add these items to your Adventure Sheet.

The cloak fits perfectly, settling over your shoulders like it was made for you. You immediately feel slightly safer, slightly more protected against the supernatural horrors that plague this place.

options.label: Close the chest and move on

success.text: The lock opens! Inside you find 40 gold pieces and a Cloak of Protection.

failure.text: The lock refuses to yield.
