Search the tavern: a journal and a bottle
A ghost's wail pierces your skull
A spectral hand passes through your chest (−3 STAMINA, −1 SKILL for good)
Lydia thanks you: the Silver Key
An old journal in shaky handwriting
A hidden laboratory behind a false wall
A Shadow drains your strength (−1 SKILL, −2 STAMINA for good)
The ritual chanting grows louder (−1 STAMINA)
Disarm a chest trap: a scroll and 50 gold
A door sealed with glowing runes
Pick the lock on an iron gate
Leave and head to the cemetery
Leave and visit the mayor's house
Walk to the edge of the village (dead end)
Behind the bar: a ledger (and a fight)

sections.text:
A Ghoul leaps from the shadows with terrifying speed! Unlike the slow, shambling zombies, Ghouls are fast, intelligent, and horrifyingly effective predators. This one's eyes glow with an unholy light, and its claws—long, curved, and sharp as razors—reach for your throat.

Special Ability - Paralyzing Touch: Each time the Ghoul successfully wounds you, you must Test your Luck. If you are Unlucky, the paralytic toxins in its claws take effect, and you lose 1 SKILL point for the remainder of this combat (cumulative—each failed test reduces your SKILL further). The paralysis makes you slower, clumsier, less effective in battle.

Fight the Ghoul!

The rope holds! You swing across the chasm, your heart in your throat as the rope creaks and the knot you tied threatens to slip. For a moment, you're suspended over darkness, over a drop that would certainly kill you if you fell.

Then your feet touch solid ground on the other side. You release the rope with shaking hands, grateful to be alive and on firm footing once more. The obstacles in your path seem determined to kill you, but your skill and luck are proving equal to the challenge—so far. {{opt:to-155}}

You discover a hidden shrine, so well concealed that you nearly missed it entirely. The entrance is behind a fallen section of wall, accessible only by crawling through a narrow gap.

Inside, the small chamber is surprisingly peaceful despite the horrors that surround it. Candles still burn—impossibly, after what must be centuries— with flames that never flicker. A small altar holds offerings: dried flowers, a silver locket, a wedding ring.

An inscription on the altar reads: "For those wronged. For those who suffer unjustly. May they find peace."

This shrine isn't dedicated to the Widow in her current form as a vengeful spirit. It's dedicated to Eliza Hollow as she was—an innocent victim, a woman whose only crime was loving the wrong man.   
You take a moment to pray at the shrine, not to any specific god, but to the concept of justice itself. The act of prayer, the moment of reflection, brings you a measure of peace and fortune.

Restore 2 LUCK (maximum of your Initial LUCK).

{{opt:to-111}}

The water is deeper than you expected, the current stronger, the cold more intense. You try to swim, but your armor weighs you down, the current pulls at you, and the water's icy grip saps your strength with terrifying speed.

{{roll}}

success.text: You swim through, exhausted but alive.

failure.text: The current pulls you under!

sections.text:
You decipher the ancient text carved into the tomb's surface, running your fingers along the weathered stone as you work to make sense of the archaic script. The language is old—centuries old—but you know enough to piece together its meaning.

The inscription reads:

"Here lies the sin of Mordecai Hollow, who betrayed the Widow on her wedding day. May his sins die with him, though we fear they will not. He murdered an innocent man and imprisoned an innocent soul. God's judgment awaits. Let any who read this know: the Hollow family's wealth was built on blood and betrayal."

The words confirm what you've been learning piece by piece—the Hollow family's dark secret, the terrible crime committed on what should have been the happiest day of Eliza's life. Mordecai Hollow murdered Thomas Ashford and bound Eliza's spirit, all for greed and ambition.

This tomb is Mordecai's—the architect of all this suffering, the man whose actions 242 years ago set in motion the curse that now threatens to consume Hollow's End and perhaps the world beyond.

Add this knowledge to your notes.

{{opt:to-388}}

sections.title: DEAD END.
sections.text:
DEAD END.

The passage ahead ends in a massive cave-in, tons of earth and stone completely blocking any forward progress. Unlike some of the other collapsed sections you've encountered, this one is absolute—there's no way through, no gap to squeeze through, no hope of digging your way past.

The sheer scale of the collapse is sobering. This must have happened years, perhaps decades ago. Stalactites have begun forming from moisture seeping through the rubble, and moss grows on some of the stones nearest to you.

You've wasted time and energy coming this way, and now you must backtrack. The frustration gnaws at you—every minute wasted is a minute closer to midnight, a minute closer to the Widow's full resurrection.

Lose 2 STAMINA from the exhausting journey to this dead end and the stress of the setback.

You have no choice but to turn back and find another route.

{{opt:to-111}}

options.label: Climb down the well on the rope

sections.text:
A Shadow's touch drains your strength in ways that go beyond mere physical damage! As its cold, insubstantial fingers brush against your skin, you feel vitality flowing out of you like water from a broken vessel. The sensation is horrifying—not pain exactly, but a profound sense of loss, of something essential being stolen.

When the Shadow pulls back, you're left feeling weaker, diminished, less capable than before. Your reflexes are slower, your strikes less accurate, your confidence shaken.

Permanently lose 1 SKILL and 2 STAMINA.

These reductions apply to both your current scores AND your maximum scores. Even if you rest or find healing, this damage cannot be undone. The Shadow has literally drained away part of what makes you a skilled warrior.

Mark these permanent reductions carefully on your Adventure Sheet.

{{opt:to-355}}

Mayor Aldric's face hardens with suspicion and fear. His eyes narrow as he studies you more carefully, and his hand moves toward something hidden beneath his desk—a weapon, most likely.

"No," he says firmly, his voice shaking but resolute. "No, I don't trust you. How do I know you're not one of them? How do I know the cult didn't send you to finish what my ancestors started?"

His paranoia isn't entirely unreasonable—in a village besieged by undead and infiltrated by dark cultists, trust is a luxury no one can afford.

"Leave!" he shouts, pulling a pistol from beneath his desk. His hand shakes, but his aim is steady enough. "Get out of my house! I won't let you trick me into helping you! LEAVE NOW!"

You have no choice but to retreat. The Mayor's fear has overcome his desperation, and without evidence to prove your intentions, you cannot convince him otherwise.

This is a critical failure. Without the Mayor's trust, you cannot obtain the SILVER KEY that he possesses—one of the three items absolutely required for victory. You've lost a valuable ally and access to a critical item.

Without the Silver Key, achieving true victory is now impossible. You can still fight the Widow, but you won't be able to properly bind her spirit. The curse will continue in some form.

{{opt:to-127}}

You manage to sneak past the guardian creature successfully, moving with the careful silence of a hunting cat. Every footstep is placed with precision, every breath controlled and quiet. Your heart hammers in your chest, but you don't let the fear show in your movements.

The guardian—a shambling undead thing that seems more instinct than intelligence—doesn't see or hear you. It continues its patrol, unaware that a living intruder has just slipped past it.

Once you're safely past and the guardian's footsteps fade into the distance, you allow yourself a moment of relief. Your muscles unclench, your breathing returns to normal, and you wipe cold sweat from your forehead.

That was too close.   
{{opt:to-301}}

A poison dart shoots from a hidden slot in the wall, whistling through the air with deadly precision! You see it at the last possible moment—a thin sliver of metal with a dark substance coating its tip.

The dart strikes home, piercing through a gap in your armor and embedding itself in your flesh. Pain flares at the impact site, followed immediately by a spreading numbness that radiates outward from the wound.

Lose 4 STAMINA from the dart wound and the poison it carries.

You pull the dart free with trembling fingers, your hand already feeling weak and unresponsive. The poison—ancient but still potent—flows through your bloodstream, making your muscles feel heavy and your reactions sluggish.

Reduce your SKILL by 1 for your next combat as the numbness affects your fighting ability. After that combat, the poison will have worked its way out of your system, and your SKILL will return to normal (unless it's been permanently reduced by other effects).

Shaken and weakened, you continue forward more carefully, your eyes scanning for additional traps.

{{opt:to-155}}

You discover a secret door hidden behind a bookshelf! The bookshelf itself is covered in dust and cobwebs, clearly undisturbed for years, but when you press against it in just the right way, it swings aside on concealed hinges to reveal a hidden room beyond.

Inside, you find an armory—or what's left of one. Most of the weapons and armor have been taken or have rusted to uselessness over the decades. But one item remains, carefully preserved in oil cloth and magical protections:

A +1 LONGSWORD

The blade is beautiful—well-balanced, perfectly weighted, and etched with faint runes that pulse with subtle magical energy. When you lift it, the sword seems to come alive in your hands, responding to your movements as if it were an extension of your own arm.

This magical weapon adds +1 to your SKILL when wielded. If you already have a magical weapon, you must choose which one to use (only one weapon can provide bonuses at a time).

Add the +1 LONGSWORD to your Adventure Sheet.

The sword feels right in your grip—like it was made for your hand, like it's been waiting here all these years just for you to claim it. {{opt:to-355}}

The floor beneath you is slick with blood—so much blood that it's pooled in the depressions between the stones, creating sticky, viscous puddles that squelch beneath your boots. The coppery smell is overwhelming, making your stomach churn.

Whose blood is this? How many people died here? The questions flash through your mind, but you don't have time to ponder them. {{roll}}

success.text: You keep your footing.

failure.text: Your foot slips in the blood!

sections.text:
The chanting grows louder—much louder. The ritual has begun! You can hear the cultists' voices raised in unison, speaking words in a language that hurts to hear, syllables that seem to twist reality itself.

You must hurry! Every second counts now. Midnight approaches, and with it, the Widow's full resurrection.

Lose 1 STAMINA as you break into a run, ignoring caution, racing through the passages toward the source of the chanting. Your lungs burn, your legs ache, but you push yourself harder.   
{{opt:to-378}}

The Zombie's grip tightens around your ankle like an iron shackle, its fingers digging into your flesh with supernatural strength. You look down and see its face—a nightmare of rot and decay, with teeth visible through holes in its cheeks and one eye hanging loose from its socket.

But it's still dangerous. Very dangerous.

Special Ability - Undead Fortitude: If you reduce this Zombie to 0 STAMINA, it may not be truly destroyed! Roll one die immediately. On a result of 5-6, the Zombie survives with 1 STAMINA and continues fighting. Its unnatural tenacity makes it refuse to stay down.

Fight the Zombie!

You find a hidden passage marked with the Hollow family crest—a shield divided into quarters, with symbols representing wealth, power, ambition, and (ironically) justice. The passage is narrow and dark, barely wide enough for one person to walk through sideways.

But it's also in remarkably good condition compared to the rest of these catacombs. Someone has maintained this passage, kept it clear of debris and collapse. Why? Where does it lead?

You follow the passage carefully, one hand on the wall for guidance, the other on your weapon. The passage winds through the earth, climbing gradually upward. After several minutes of careful navigation, you emerge into a different location entirely—what appears to be the basement of the Hollow manor itself!

This secret passage provides a direct route from the catacombs to the manor, bypassing the cemetery entirely. It's both convenient and deeply suspicious—why would the Hollow family need such a passage? What dark business required secret access between the manor and the catacombs?

{{opt:to-301}}

A spectral figure materializes before you—translucent, glowing faintly, more suggestion than substance. Unlike other hostile spirits you've encountered, this one doesn't attack. Instead, it simply stands there, its sad eyes fixed upon you.

Then it raises one arm and points toward a section of wall that looks no different from any other. Its mouth moves as if speaking, but you hear only the faintest whisper: "True name..."

Then it fades, dissipating like morning mist under sunlight, leaving you alone with its cryptic message and the direction it indicated.

You approach the wall it pointed to and examine it carefully. At first, you find nothing. Then your fingers detect a slight depression—a hidden catch. You press it, and a section of wall swings inward, revealing a hidden chamber beyond.

The ghost was trying to help you! Perhaps it was one of Eliza's servants, someone who knew the truth, someone who wants the curse ended as much as the living do.

Add 1 LUCK for this fortunate (if eerie) assistance.

{{opt:to-335}}

sections.title: INSTANT DEATH!
sections.text:
INSTANT DEATH!

The floor gives way beneath you, and you plummet into a bottomless pit! The darkness swallows you whole as you fall, fall, fall into depths that seem to have no end.

Your screams echo off walls you can't see, growing fainter and more distant until they fade entirely. Perhaps you fall forever, trapped in an eternal descent. Perhaps you eventually hit bottom, but by then you're traveling so fast that death is instantaneous and mercifully painless.

Either way, your adventure ends here, lost in the depths beneath Hollow's End. Your body will never be recovered. Your name will be forgotten. The curse continues, and the village remains doomed.   
THE END

You successfully disarm the trap, your skilled hands finding and disabling the mechanism before it can trigger. The chest opens smoothly, revealing treasures within:

50 Gold Pieces - A small fortune, carefully hoarded by someone long dead.

SCROLL OF PROTECTION - A magical scroll inscribed with protective wards. You can use this scroll once during any combat to gain +2 to all saving throws for that entire battle. Once used, the scroll crumbles to dust.

Add these items to your Adventure Sheet.

Satisfied with your haul and proud of your trap-disarming skills, you continue your exploration.

{{opt:to-301}}

The cultist leader rises to his feet, raising his ceremonial dagger high above his head. His eyes burn with fanatical fervor as he begins chanting in a dark tongue. The other cultists turn toward you, their numbers suddenly seeming far more threatening.

You've triggered an alarm, and now you must face their leader!

Special Ability - Dark Magic: Once per combat, the Cult Fanatic may attempt to cast a Command spell. Roll one die. On a result of 5-6, the spell succeeds, and you are magically compelled to stand still for one Attack Round. You lose your entire attack for that round (the Fanatic still gets to attack you normally).

This enemy is dangerous—both skilled with his blade and capable of dark magic.

Fight for your life!

You discover the Mayor's secret journal, hidden in a locked drawer in his desk. The lock is simple enough to pick or force, and once you have the journal in hand, you flip through its pages eagerly.

The entries are written in a shaking hand, the words often smudged as if the writer was crying while he wrote:

"I've discovered the truth about what my great-great-grandfather did. The wedding massacre. The murder of Thomas Ashford. The binding of Eliza's spirit. All of it true. All of it unforgivable.

We thought we could escape the consequences of our ancestors' sins. We were wrong. The curse grows stronger each year, each generation. Soon it will break free completely.

The guilt haunts me. I see her sometimes, in mirrors, in windows, in the shadows of my own room—the Widow, still wearing her blood-stained wedding dress, her eyes filled with rage and pain.

I don't know how to break the curse. The journals say only the Widow's true name and silver can bind her again. But even if we bind her, is that justice? Haven't we tormented her enough?

May God forgive us. May someone braver than I find the strength to end this nightmare."

The journal confirms what you've been learning—and provides additional context about the Mayor's own guilt and fear.   
{{opt:to-388}}

options.label: Speak the counter-spell from the Alchemist's Journal

sections.text:
You manage to sneak closer to the ritual chamber, moving through the shadows with practiced stealth. The cultists are so focused on their dark ceremony that they don't notice your approach.

From your new vantage point, you can see everything: the summoning circle drawn in blood, the candles arranged in occult patterns, the ritual implements, and most importantly, the girl chained in the center—Mayor Aldric's daughter, Lydia.

The cultists are chanting in unison, their voices rising and falling in disturbing patterns that seem to make the very air vibrate. You realize with horror that the ritual is already underway—though not yet complete. You still have time to interrupt it, to save the girl and disrupt whatever dark magic they're weaving.

But you must act carefully. One wrong move could alert them to your presence.

{{opt:to-245}}

The potion explodes without warning! The glass vial shatters in your hands, and the liquid inside ignites with a roar of flame and a blast of concussive force that throws you backward.

Lose 3 STAMINA from the explosion—burns on your hands and face, bruises from being thrown against the wall, and the general trauma of having a magical explosive detonate in your grip.

You lie on the ground for a moment, ears ringing, vision swimming, trying to understand what just happened. The potion was either trapped, or unstable, or perhaps you simply handled it wrong. Either way, the result is the same—pain and injury.

Once you can stand again, you continue, more wary now of mysterious liquids in glass bottles.

{{opt:to-156}}

You find a wounded villager hiding in a side passage, clutching a terrible wound in his side. His face is pale from blood loss, his breathing shallow and rapid. When he sees you, hope flickers in his eyes.

"Help... me..." he gasps out. "Attacked... by undead... barely escaped..."

You kneel beside him, assessing his injuries. They're serious, but not immediately fatal if he gets help soon. You do what you can—tearing cloth for bandages, applying pressure to the worst wounds, speaking reassuringly.

"The Widow," he whispers urgently, gripping your arm with surprising strength. "She rises at midnight. Only silver... only silver can bind her. The old rituals... they knew... silver binds the dead..."

He presses something into your hand—a small leather pouch. "Take this... use it... stop her..."

Inside the pouch, you find 20 Gold Pieces—likely all the wealth this man possessed.

Add 20 Gold Pieces to your Adventure Sheet.

His grip loosens, his eyes close, and his breathing slows. You think perhaps he's dying, but then you feel a faint pulse. He's unconscious but alive. You make him as comfortable as possible and move on—you can't help him further, but you can avenge him by stopping the curse.   
{{opt:to-127}}

options.label: Investigate what is in the water
Go back and find another route

sections.text:
You're suddenly attacked by a swarm of diseased rats! They pour from cracks in the walls like a furry flood, their eyes gleaming red in the darkness, their teeth yellow and sharp.

The rats bite at your ankles, crawl up your legs, try to get under your armor. Their bites are numerous and painful, and worse—the rats carry disease.

Lose 2 STAMINA from the numerous bites.

Reduce your SKILL by 1 temporarily as fever and infection begin to take hold. This SKILL reduction lasts until you can rest properly or find magical healing.

You fight off the rat swarm by stamping, swinging your weapon, and generally making yourself as dangerous and unappetizing as possible. Eventually, they scatter back into their holes, leaving you bitten, bleeding, and feeling distinctly unwell.

{{opt:to-221}}

You discover an ancient tapestry hanging on the wall, surprisingly well-preserved despite the dampness and decay that permeates this place. The fabric is thick and heavy, woven with skill that speaks of master craftsmanship.

The scene depicted is horrifying: a wedding ceremony turned massacre. You can see the bride in her white dress, the groom at the altar, and armed men bursting through the doors with swords drawn. The next panel shows the groom falling, blood spreading across white marble. The final panel shows the bride screaming, her dress now stained red, while shadowy figures bind her with silver chains.

At the bottom of the tapestry, carefully embroidered letters spell out a name: ELIZA HOLLOW

This is her—the Widow. This tapestry depicts the moment her life ended and her eternal torment began. Seeing it laid out so explicitly, the horror of what was done to her becomes even more real, more visceral.

The tapestry confirms the legend and provides the Widow's true name if you didn't already know it.

{{opt:to-301}}

sections.title: DEAD END.
sections.text:
DEAD END.

This path leads to the very edge of the village—the boundary beyond which lies only wilderness and the open road you traveled to reach Hollow's End. There's nothing here that can help you, no passage forward, no secrets to uncover.

You've wasted time exploring a path that leads nowhere useful. Frustrated, you turn back toward the village proper. {{opt:to-1}} (you're back at the village entrance).

"I've heard rumors of undead plaguing this village," you say carefully, watching the bartender's reaction. "What can you tell me about it?"

The bartender's smile widens—impossibly wide, far wider than any human mouth should stretch. It keeps widening until you can see rows and rows of teeth, far too many teeth, teeth that are suddenly sharp as needles.

"The dead walk," he says, and now his voice is layered, multiple voices speaking in unison. "Very unfortunate for the living. Perhaps you should speak with the Mayor before you—"

He stops mid-sentence. His head tilts at an unnatural angle, like a puppet whose strings have been jerked wrong. His eyes go completely black, the pupils expanding to swallow the whites, swallow the iris, swallow everything until they're like looking into two pools of absolute darkness.

"Before you JOIN them!" he snarls, and his form begins to ripple and shift. Skin flows like water, bones crack and reform, height changes, proportions distort.

This is no human bartender. It's a Doppelganger—a shapeshifting creature that kills and replaces its victims, wearing their faces like masks. The real bartender is probably dead... or imprisoned somewhere.

The Doppelganger lunges at you with inhuman speed!

Special Ability - Shapechanger: After the Doppelganger takes damage, it may Test its Luck (you roll for it). If Lucky, it shifts forms rapidly, confusing you. Reduce your Attack Strength by 2 for the next Attack Round only as you struggle to track which form is real and which is illusion.

Fight for your life!
You attempt to flee before combat begins, your survival instincts overriding your courage. Sometimes, discretion truly is the better part of valor. {{roll}}

success.text: You escape before it can engage you.

failure.text: It catches you and forces a fight.

sections.text:
You drink from the ancient fountain, hoping the water might be blessed or possess healing properties. The water is cold and clear, tasting faintly metallic but not unpleasant.

{{roll}}

success.text: The water is blessed!

failure.text: The water is cursed!

options.label: Leave the candles burning and move on

sections.text:
You find a skeleton clutching a diary in its bony hands, the book held so tightly that you have to pry the fingers loose to retrieve it. The skeleton is sitting with its back against the wall, as if it simply sat down here to rest and never got up again.

The diary is written in a shaking hand that grows increasingly erratic as the entries progress:

"Day 12 of captivity: The Widow's wail is stronger tonight. It pierces the walls, pierces my ears, pierces my very mind. I cannot sleep. Day 13: Sleep deprivation is taking its toll. I hear things that aren't there. See shadows that move when I'm not looking. The food is almost gone.

Day 14: They're at the door. I can hear them scratching, moaning, calling my name in voices of the dead. I've barricaded myself in, but I know it won't hold forever. If anyone finds this—tell my family I love them. Tell them I—"

The entry ends abruptly, unfinished. You look at the skeleton with new understanding. This person died here, trapped and alone, listening to the undead trying to break through the door.

The diary provides no useful information beyond a chilling reminder of the curse's lethality.

{{opt:to-127}}

A cultist emerges from the shadows, drawing a wicked-looking ceremonial dagger from beneath his robes. His face is hidden beneath a deep hood, but you can see his lips moving in silent prayer—or perhaps a curse aimed at you.

Special Quality - Fanatic: This cultist fights to the death with no thought of surrender or self-preservation. He cannot be intimidated or reasoned with.

Fight the cultist!

You successfully pick the lock on the iron gate, using whatever tools you have at hand or improvising with bits of wire and your own dexterity. The lock is old and corroded, which actually works in your favor—the mechanism is stiff but predictable.

After several tense minutes of careful manipulation, you hear a satisfying click. The lock opens, and the gate swings aside with a rusty groan.

Beyond the gate, a passage leads deeper underground, sloping downward into darkness. The air that flows from below is cold and carries the scent of earth and water.

{{opt:to-155}}

The Shadow's touch is brief but devastating! For just a moment, its cold, insubstantial form makes contact with yours, and in that instant, something vital is ripped away from you.

You stagger back, gasping, feeling fundamentally changed. Your movements are clumsier, your reflexes slower, your sense of balance off. The Shadow has drained something essential from you—not just strength, but the very skill that makes you a competent warrior.

Permanently lose 1 SKILL.

This reduction applies to both your current and maximum SKILL scores. Even rest and healing cannot restore what the Shadow has stolen. Mark this permanent reduction on your Adventure Sheet carefully.

{{opt:to-355}}

You find a section of wall that looks climbable—rough stone with enough handholds and footholds to make ascending possible. The climb looks dangerous, but it also looks like it might bypass whatever obstacles lie on the ground-level path.

You begin climbing carefully, testing each handhold before trusting your weight to it. The stone is rough under your hands, cutting your palms, but you make steady progress upward.

After several tense minutes of climbing, you reach the top—a ledge that overlooks the area below. From this vantage point, you can see far more than you could from ground level.

Most importantly, you can see the Hollow manor in the distance. It looks ghostly and translucent even from here, shimmering like a mirage. That's where you need to go eventually—where the final confrontation awaits.

{{opt:to-301}}
A trap activates as you step on a hidden pressure plate! Spears shoot from slots in the walls, whistling through the air with deadly precision. {{roll}}

success.text: You dodge the spears.

failure.text: A spear catches you!

sections.text:
You find a prayer book clutched in a skeleton's hands. The skeleton is kneeling as if in prayer, its bones arranged in a position of supplication. Perhaps this person spent their final moments praying for salvation that never came.

The prayer book itself is old but well-preserved, its pages filled with prayers to various gods and protective verses. One passage has been circled repeatedly, as if the skeleton read it over and over:

"Grant strength to those who face darkness. Grant courage to those who stand against evil. Grant protection to those who defend the innocent." Reading the prayers, you feel a sense of peace and spiritual fortification. The book seems to radiate a faint protective energy.

For your next combat ONLY, gain +1 SKILL and +1 LUCK. These bonuses apply only to the next battle you fight, then fade. The prayer book's blessing is temporary but powerful.

Mark this temporary bonus on your Adventure Sheet (and remember to remove it after your next combat).

{{opt:to-127}}

The water ahead is far deeper than you expected—rising from ankle-deep to waist-deep to chest-deep in just a few steps. The cold is shocking, like being plunged into ice water. Your armor weighs you down, making swimming difficult or impossible.

Do you have ROPE in your inventory?

If yes, you have rope: You quickly tie the rope around your waist, securing the other end to a solid pillar. This makeshift safety line will keep you from being swept away by any current. {{opt:to-221}} (but with the confidence that you have a safety measure).

If no rope: You'll have to risk it. {{roll}}

options.label: Wade across, secured by the Rope

roll.label: Wade across without a rope (Test your Luck)

success.text: You wade through without incident.

failure.text: The current is stronger than you realized!

sections.text:
You notice fresh boot prints in the dust on the floor—recent tracks, certainly made within the last few hours. Someone else is (or was) in these catacombs recently.

The tracks lead toward the manor, suggesting that whoever made them was heading in the same direction you need to go. Could be a cultist. Could be another adventurer. Could be something else entirely.

The prints are humanoid but the stride is oddly regular, almost mechanical. Whatever made these tracks walks with unnatural precision. This information might prove useful later. At minimum, it tells you that you're not alone down here.

{{opt:to-301}}

sections.title: The Widow appears before you without warning!
sections.text:
The Widow appears before you without warning!

One moment, the corridor is empty. The next, she's simply there—a tall figure in a blood-stained wedding dress, her face hidden beneath a torn veil, her hands reaching toward you with clawed fingers.

"You dare enter MY domain?" her voice echoes, seeming to come from everywhere at once. It's not a human voice—it's the sound of wind through empty halls, of chains dragging on stone, of anguish given voice.

She sees you. She knows you're here to stop her. And she's ready to end you.

This could be your final confrontation—do you have what you need to bind her?

Do you have the SILVER KEY and do you know her TRUE NAME?

If yes, you have both: You might be able to bind her properly! {{opt:to-395}}

If no, you're missing one or both: You'll have to fight or flee, but you cannot properly bind her spirit. {{opt:to-362}}

options.label: Bind her with the Silver Key and her true name
Fight or flee: you are missing the key or her name

sections.text:
You sit down and consume one of your Provisions, taking a much-needed rest to eat and regain your strength. The simple act of eating, of taking care of your body's basic needs, feels almost luxurious in this place of death and horror.

The food is simple but nourishing—dried meat, hard bread, maybe some cheese or dried fruit. Your body craves the sustenance after the exertions and stresses of your journey.

Restore 4 STAMINA (maximum of your Initial STAMINA).

Cross off 1 Provision from your Adventure Sheet.

Feeling somewhat refreshed, you prepare to continue your exploration.

{{opt:to-155}}

sections.title: The door ahead is locked tight, secured with a heavy iron lock that looks formidable.

options.label: Unlock the door with the Brass Key

success.text: The lock gives way.

failure.text: The door will not budge.

sections.title: You find a journal entry written in a trembling hand:
sections.text:
You find a journal entry written in a trembling hand:

"Day 7 of captivity: The Wight in the eastern chamber has been released by the cultists. It feeds on fear and despair. I can feel it even through the walls—a presence of pure malevolence.

According to the old texts, only blessed silver can truly harm it. Normal weapons will slow it down, but it will keep regenerating unless struck with consecrated metal.

If anyone finds this—beware the Wight. It drains more than life. It drains hope itself."

The journal provides valuable intelligence about the Wight you may face (or may have already faced). Blessed or silver weapons are most effective against it.

Add this information to your notes.

{{opt:to-267}}

A ghost materializes before you, its translucent form taking the rough shape of a person—though its features are blurred and indistinct, as if seen through thick fog.

It doesn't attack. Instead, it speaks in a voice like wind through reeds: "Silver key... true name... midnight bell..."

The words are cryptic but clearly meant to help. These are the components of the ritual to bind the Widow: a silver key for the binding, her true name to invoke her properly, and the midnight bell as the timing mechanism.

The ghost fades away before you can ask questions, dissipating like morning mist.

Add this cryptic information to your notes if you haven't already figured it out.

{{opt:to-335}}

You attempt to cross a crumbling bridge that spans a dark chasm. The bridge is ancient, its wooden planks rotted and its rope supports frayed to the point of breaking.

You step carefully onto the first plank, testing your weight. It holds. You take another step. Still holding. Encouraged, you continue across, moving slowly and carefully, distributing your weight as evenly as possible.

The bridge creaks and groans beneath you, but it holds together—barely. Each step is an exercise in faith and balance, but you make it to the other side without incident.

Exhaling with relief, you step onto solid ground and continue.

{{opt:to-155}}

You find a healing shrine—a small alcove where candles still burn (impossibly, after all these years) and a stone basin holds crystal-clear water that seems to glow with its own inner light.

This is a place of power, a sacred space that has somehow remained untouched by the corruption spreading through the catacombs. Perhaps the gods still watch over this small corner, or perhaps some ancient magic protects it.

You approach the shrine respectfully and drink from the basin. The water tastes pure and sweet, and you feel its healing power flowing through you immediately.

Restore all STAMINA to your Initial value.

Add 1 LUCK for discovering this blessed place.

You take a moment to rest here, feeling safer than you have since entering Hollow's End. The shrine radiates peace and protection. When you're ready, you continue your quest renewed in body and spirit.

{{opt:to-301}}

You defeat the cultist, and as he falls, something drops from his robes—a medallion bearing the cult's symbol. The symbol is a twisted version of the Hollow family crest, corrupted and inverted, with additional occult markings added.

This medallion might prove useful. If you wear it, other cultists might mistake you for one of their own—at least briefly. Add the CULT MEDALLION to your Adventure Sheet.

Wearing this medallion could allow you to bluff your way past cultists or overhear their plans without being detected. But it's also dangerous—if they see through your deception, they'll attack with extra fury for your blasphemy.

{{opt:to-180}}

You descend carefully into the old well, hand over hand on the rope you've secured. The walls are slick with moisture and slime, making the climb treacherous. The darkness below seems to swallow your lantern light.

Finally, your feet touch bottom—water, about ankle-deep and cold as ice. You're standing in what appears to be an ancient cistern or storage chamber.

Your search of the area reveals:

30 Gold Pieces scattered in the water (perhaps tossed down here as offerings or lost over the years)

POTION OF STRENGTH - A red liquid in a crystal vial. When drunk before combat, this potion grants +2 SKILL for one combat only.Add these items to your Adventure Sheet.

Satisfied with your haul, you climb back up the rope to ground level.

{{opt:to-127}}

options.label: Go to the left passage (toward the chanting)
Go to the right passage (the flooded section)
Go to the straight ahead passage (toward candlelight)

sections.text:
The Skeleton Warrior crumbles under your final blow, its bones collapsing into a pile of dust and fragments. The dark magic that animated it disperses like smoke in wind, and you're left standing over the remains of something that should have stayed buried.

As you search through the bone pile, something glints in the dim light—a golden ring, still on what remains of the skeleton's finger bone. You pull it free and examine it. The craftsmanship is exquisite, and the gold is pure. This ring is worth a considerable sum.

Add 40 Gold Pieces worth of value to your Adventure Sheet (you can sell the ring later, or keep it as a valuable item). With the guardian defeated and the treasure claimed, you continue deeper into the catacombs.

{{opt:to-155}}

The passage ahead narrows dramatically, forcing you to turn sideways and shuffle through. The walls press in from both sides, and the ceiling lowers until you're hunched over. Your armor scrapes against stone with sounds that seem impossibly loud in the confined space.

Claustrophobia begins to claw at your mind. What if you get stuck? What if the passage gets even narrower? What if the ceiling collapses? {{roll}}

success.text: You squeeze through the crawl space.

failure.text: You become stuck, and work yourself free.

sections.text:
You discover a weapons rack mounted on the wall, surprisingly well-preserved considering the decay that surrounds it. Most of the weapons have rusted into uselessness, but one item catches your eye:

A SILVER DAGGER

The blade gleams even in the dim light, untarnished by time. Silver is particularly effective against undead creatures, and you sense that this weapon will prove invaluable in the battles ahead.   
Add the SILVER DAGGER to your Adventure Sheet.

When wielded, this dagger deals +1 extra damage against all undead creatures (so you'll deal 3 damage on successful hits instead of the normal 2). Against living enemies, it functions as a normal dagger.

Silver binds the dead—this is a truth you're coming to understand more deeply with each discovery.

{{opt:to-301}}

The Zombie's bite is deep and terrible! Its diseased teeth tear through your flesh, and you can feel corruption flooding into your bloodstream through the wound. The pain is immediate and intense, but worse is the spreading numbness and fever that follows.

Lose 3 STAMINA from the bite wound itself.

Additionally, reduce your maximum STAMINA by 1 permanently. The Zombie's bite carries a supernatural disease that weakens you fundamentally. Even if you heal the immediate wound, you've lost part of your vitality forever.

Mark both the current STAMINA loss and the permanent maximum reduction on your Adventure Sheet.

Despite the terrible wound, you continue fighting.

{{opt:to-298}}

You discover a hidden library room, concealed behind a section of wall that looks no different from any other until you notice the subtle seam and the hidden catch. Inside, shelves filled with ancient books line the walls—grimoires, histories, journals, and texts on subjects both mundane and arcane.

This library contains crucial information about the curse, the Hollow family history, and the rituals used to bind and unbind spirits. You spend several minutes quickly scanning the most relevant texts, absorbing as much information as possible.

The knowledge you gain here could mean the difference between success and failure in your quest.

Add 2 LUCK for this incredible discovery. Sometimes, knowledge truly is power.

Add "Library Knowledge: Curse History" to your notes.

{{opt:to-355}}
The floor suddenly collapses beneath you! Ancient wood and rotted supports finally give way after centuries of bearing weight. {{roll}}

outcomes.text: The collapse is catastrophic! Test your Luck to catch the edge.

success.text: You catch the edge as the floor falls away, badly hurt.

failure.text: You fall into the spike pit below!

outcomes.text: You catch yourself at the last moment.
You leap back just in time.

sections.text:
A spectral voice echoes through the chamber, seeming to come from everywhere and nowhere at once. The voice is hollow, distant, like someone calling from the bottom of a deep well:

"Beware... beware midnight... when the bell tolls twelve... when the binding breaks... when vengeance comes..." Then silence. The voice doesn't return, no matter how long you wait.

The warning is cryptic but clear enough—midnight is the critical moment. Whatever you're going to do, you must do it before the clock strikes twelve.

{{opt:to-301}}

You find a torn page from what appears to be the Alchemist's Journal—perhaps torn out during a hasty departure or a struggle. The page is crumpled and bloodstained, but the text is still legible:

"The Widow is bound by silver chains and dark magic, but the binding is imperfect. It was never meant to last forever—only long enough for the guilty generation to die in peace.

To properly seal her spirit for eternity requires three components: silver forged specifically for binding (such as the Silver Key), her true name spoken with authority, and the ritual performed at the moment of greatest supernatural power (midnight on the anniversary of her binding).

Without all three components, the binding will be temporary at best. The Widow will eventually break free again, perhaps even more powerful than before."

This information confirms what you've been piecing together from various sources. You need the Silver Key, the true name, and proper timing. Add this knowledge to your notes.

{{opt:to-355}}

The Zombie lets go of your ankle
A trapped corridor, safely passed (+1 LUCK)
A hidden laboratory: the journal and the Widow's name

Climb a shaft to the surface
A Skeleton Warrior guards the passage (fight)

sections.text:
You drink the mysterious potion, and immediately you feel... lucky. The sensation is hard to describe—like the universe has shifted slightly in your favor, like probability itself has bent toward your benefit.

This is a POTION OF LUCK!

Add 3 to your LUCK (maximum of Initial LUCK +2). So if your Initial LUCK was 10, you can now go up to 12.

This substantial boost to your fortune could prove crucial in the challenges ahead. Sometimes, luck is just as important as skill or strength. {{opt:to-301}}

You find a map of the catacombs etched into the wall—probably carved by some long-dead explorer who wanted to leave a record of the labyrinth's layout. The map is crude but detailed enough to be useful.

Studying it carefully, you begin to understand the overall structure of this underground maze. You can see where you are, where you've been, and— most importantly—where you might need to go.

Add 1 LUCK for this fortunate discovery. Knowledge of the terrain is invaluable.

Add "Catacomb Map" to your notes.

{{opt:to-155}}

The Shadow drains your life force before dissipating completely! Even in its final moments, it manages to steal something vital from you—not just health, but fundamental vitality and skill.

Permanently lose 1 SKILL and 2 maximum STAMINA.

These reductions cannot be healed or restored by any normal means. The Shadow has taken part of your life essence with it into whatever dark realm spawned it.

Mark these permanent reductions carefully on your Adventure Sheet.

Weakened but alive, you continue forward.

{{opt:to-355}}

sections.title: You discover a journal with critical information about the curse's timeline:
sections.text:
You discover a journal with critical information about the curse's timeline:

"Midnight approaches. The Widow's power grows with each passing hour. By the time the midnight bell tolls, she will have reached her full strength. Only silver and her true name can stop her then. Without both, she will be unstoppable."

The journal's warning is clear: time is running out. Every minute wasted is a minute closer to the Widow's complete resurrection. Add this timing information to your notes.

{{opt:to-378}}

You find a silver locket lying on the ground, its chain broken. Opening it carefully, you discover a miniature painting inside—a wedding portrait. The bride is beautiful, her smile radiant with joy. The groom looks at her with obvious adoration.

On the back of the locket, engraved in flowing script, are the words: "Eliza Hollow, my beloved bride. Forever yours, Thomas Ashford."

This is the Widow's locket—a token of the love she shared with the man murdered on their wedding day. Seeing this reminder of her happiness before tragedy struck makes her story even more heartbreaking.

Add "Eliza's Locket" to your inventory if you wish to keep it. It may prove useful later.

{{opt:to-388}}

A cultist sounds the alarm! His shout echoes through the catacombs: "Intruder! Intruder in the sacred halls! Brothers, to arms!" You hear the sound of running footsteps—multiple sets, coming from different directions. More cultists are approaching rapidly! You can't fight them all. You must flee!

{{opt:to-221}}

You successfully pick the lock on a heavy chest, your skilled fingers manipulating the mechanism until you hear a satisfying click. The lid opens to reveal treasures within:

CLOAK OF SHADOWS - A dark garment that seems to absorb light rather than reflect it. When worn, this cloak adds +2 to all stealth attempts and makes you significantly harder to detect in shadows or darkness.

Add the CLOAK OF SHADOWS to your Adventure Sheet.

If you choose to wear it, the cloak settles over your shoulders like a piece of living darkness, wrapping you in concealment. {{opt:to-301}}

options.label: Turn back and find another route

sections.text:
A Specter materializes without warning, its form translucent and glowing with pale blue light! Unlike the Phantom Servants you've encountered, this spirit seems more powerful, more malevolent, more independent.

It fixes its hollow eyes upon you and opens its mouth in a silent scream that you somehow still hear in your mind.

Special Ability - Incorporeal: As a ghostly entity, normal weapons deal only 1 damage instead of 2. Magical or silver weapons deal normal damage.

Fight the Phantom Servant!

You find a HEALING POTION hidden in a small alcove! The glass vial contains luminous red liquid that glows with its own inner light—a sure sign of magical healing properties.

Add HEALING POTION to your Adventure Sheet (restores 6 STAMINA when drunk).

This potion could save your life in a critical moment. Guard it well.

{{opt:to-155}}

The ancient bridge groans under your weight but holds together—barely. You can hear wood cracking, feel the structure swaying, but you make it across without incident.

On the far side, you pause to catch your breath and let your heart rate return to normal. That was closer than you'd like to admit. {{opt:to-155}}

You discover a secret shrine dedicated to the Widow—but not as the vengeful spirit she's become. This shrine honors her as she was: Eliza Hollow, innocent victim.

The shrine is simple but touching: candles that burn with steady flames (impossible after so many years, yet here they are), fresh flowers (equally impossible, yet present), and offerings of jewelry and coins. Someone—perhaps many people over the years—has maintained this shrine in secret.

An inscription reads: "Honor Eliza, wronged on her wedding day. May she find peace. May love triumph over hate. May the innocent be remembered."

This shrine wasn't created by cultists serving the dark Widow. This was made by people who mourned Eliza, who recognized the injustice done to her, who hoped for her peace rather than her vengeance.

Add "Secret Shrine to Eliza" to your notes.

{{opt:to-388}}

options.label: Find a skeleton with a diary
Discover a journal about the curse

success.text: You are ready for what is coming.

Black candles arranged in a circle cast flickering shadows across the walls. In the center sits an ancient altar stained with blood—centuries of blood, layer upon layer. Strange symbols pulse with dark energy around the altar's perimeter, and the air itself seems thick with malevolence.

If you don't have the ledger: The symbols are meaningless to you—just mysterious markings on ancient stone. {{opt:to-104}} (examine the ritual book).

Destroy the altar to weaken the curse ({{opt:to-80}})

You step into the cemetery, and the mist immediately swirls up around your ankles like grasping fingers made of cold vapor. As the mist clears slightly, your worst fears are realized—you're surrounded!

Three Zombies emerge from freshly opened graves, their moaning filling the air with sounds of hunger and mindless rage. But these aren't the only threats. Perched on a gravestone like some grotesque gargoyle sits a Ghoul, its eyes glowing with unholy intelligence, its long claws clicking together in anticipation. This creature is far more dangerous than the Zombies—faster, smarter, and equipped with paralytic toxins in its claws.

You must fight them all! The Zombies first, one at a time, and then the cunning Ghoul.

All Zombies have Undead Fortitude: When reduced to 0 STAMINA, roll one die. On 5-6, they survive with 1 STAMINA. After defeating all three Zombies, you must immediately fight:

Ghoul's Paralyzing Touch: Each time the Ghoul wounds you, Test your Luck. If Unlucky, the toxins take effect and you lose 1 SKILL for the remainder of this combat (cumulative—each failed test makes you weaker).

If your STAMINA drops to 4 or less during battle: You may attempt to flee. Test your Luck.

You enter the Spectral Manor proper. The walls shimmer and phase between solid and translucent, between real and ghostly. Through the semi transparent walls, you can see ghostly scenes playing out like memories trapped in time:

A wedding ceremony in progress, beautiful and joyful

The same ceremony interrupted by violence, blood spreading across white flowers

A bride screaming in anguish as her husband falls

The bride being dragged away by armed men

Silver chains wrapping around a spectral form

And then... nothing but rage and darkness

These are the Widow's memories, replaying endlessly in the fabric of the manor itself.

The grand entrance hall has three doorways:

Left doorway: You can see into what appears to be a ballroom where ghostly figures dance eternally to music you can't hear, trapped in their final moments of joy before the curse consumed them.

Center doorway: A grand staircase ascends into darkness, its steps worn smooth by centuries of footsteps.

Right doorway: A corridor lined with portraits, though every face has been scratched out with furious claws, as if the Widow herself destroyed the images of the Hollow family in her rage.

You've successfully fought your way through the undead and cultist-infested catacombs. Your path has been treacherous, your battles many, but you're still standing.

Before you, the passage opens into what can only be described as the threshold between the world of the living and the realm of the dead. The Spectral Manor awaits—a building that exists partially in both worlds, held together by the Widow's rage and dark magic.

The time for the final confrontation approaches. Do you have everything you need?

Check your inventory:

Do you have the SILVER KEY? (Critical for binding)

Do you know the Widow's TRUE NAME? (Eliza Hollow)

Do you understand that midnight is when you must perform the binding?

If you have all three pieces of crucial knowledge, victory is possible. If you're missing any, the final battle will be far more difficult—perhaps impossible.

Steel yourself. The Widow waits ahead, and she's been waiting for 242 years to unleash her vengeance.

The manor itself seems to pulse with malevolent energy, its walls shifting between solid and ghostly, between the real world and some darker realm. You can feel the Widow's presence like a weight pressing down on you, watching you, waiting for you.   
This is it. The final confrontation approaches. Every decision you've made, every item you've gathered, every ally you've helped—all of it has led to this moment.

Are you ready to face the Widow and end the Curse of Hollow's End?

sections.title: The Binding Wavers
sections.text:
The binding wavers! You must fight the Widow herself before the ritual can complete.

Special: Wail of the Forsaken - At combat start, Test Luck or reduce SKILL by 2 for entire battle. Spectral Form - Immune to normal weapons (must have magical weapon).

You push open the massive doors to the Widow's lair, and the temperature plummets instantly. Your breath forms ice crystals that fall like snow. The chamber beyond is vast—the manor's grand ballroom, now transformed into the heart of darkness itself.

The Widow stands in the center of the room, waiting for you. She's terrible and beautiful in equal measure—a tall figure in a wedding dress stained with 242 years of blood. Her face is hidden beneath a torn veil, but you can feel her hollow eyes fixed upon you with recognition and rage.

"So," her voice echoes from everywhere and nowhere, layered with the screams of the dead, "another fool comes to stop me. Another hero seeking to prevent my righteous vengeance. Do you know what they did to me? Do you know what I suffered?"

You can see the pain beneath the rage, the human woman trapped inside the monster.

"I was going to be HAPPY!" she shrieks, her form expanding, becoming more terrible. "I was going to have a LIFE! They murdered my husband! They CHAINED my spirit! They left me in darkness for TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO YEARS! And you... you dare try to imprison me again?"

Three Shadows tear themselves from the darkness, manifestations of her rage. They rush toward you, cold and terrible. Do you have the SILVER KEY and know her TRUE NAME (Eliza Hollow)?

If YES - you have both: Continue below for the proper binding ritual.

If NO - you're missing one or both: {{opt:to-362}} (incomplete confrontation).

THE PROPER BINDING RITUAL:

You hold up the SILVER KEY with one hand while your other hand clutches whatever protective amulets you carry to your chest. Drawing upon every ounce of courage and strength you possess, you shout with absolute authority:

"ELIZA HOLLOW! I bind you by your true name, by this silver seal forged for spirit-binding, and by the ancient laws that govern the dead! Your curse ends TONIGHT!"

The effect is immediate and dramatic.

The Widow freezes in mid-air, her spectral form rippling as if struck by invisible force. Her hollow eyes widen with shock, recognition, and—could it be?—hope. The SILVER KEY blazes with brilliant white light so bright you must squint.

Chains of pure silver energy materialize from the very air, wrapping around the Widow's form like ethereal rope. Each chain blazes with the same white light as the key.

"NO!" she wails, but her voice is different now—less rage, more desperation. "Not again! I will have my REVENGE!" But her power is failing. The three Shadows dissipate like smoke. The temperature begins to rise.

sections.title: COMPLETE VICTORY!
sections.text:
COMPLETE VICTORY!

You continue speaking the name with absolute conviction, each repetition strengthening the binding: "Eliza Hollow. Eliza Hollow. ELIZA HOLLOW!"

The AMULET OF THE GRAVE (if you found it) glows warm against your chest, absorbing the dark energy that flows from the Widow like poison being drawn from a wound. Each strand of rage, each thread of vengeance, is pulled into the amulet and neutralized.

With each repetition of her name, the silver chains grow brighter and tighter. The Widow's form begins to change before your eyes:

The blood staining her dress fades

Her hollow eyes fill with color—beautiful hazel eyes that once sparkled with life

Her rage-twisted features soften, returning to the beauty she possessed in life

Her clawed hands become delicate fingers

"Eliza," you say one final time, but gently now, with compassion rather than command.

She shimmers, becoming more translucent, more peaceful. For just a moment, you see her as she truly was: a beautiful young woman on her wedding day, smiling with pure joy.

A single tear rolls down her cheek, leaving a trail of silver light.

"Thank you," she whispers, her voice no longer the inhuman wail that chilled your blood. It's simply the voice of a woman who has been in pain for too long. "Thank you for remembering my name. Thank you for setting me free."

"Where is Thomas?" she asks, looking around as if seeing clearly for the first time in centuries.

And then she sees him.

A second ghostly form materializes—Thomas Ashford, waiting patiently for 242 years, ready to finally take his bride's hand. He wears wedding clothes that are no longer stained with blood, and his eyes are filled with love.

Eliza's face transforms with joy so pure it hurts to witness. She reaches out, and Thomas takes her hand. Where their fingers touch, golden light blooms—warm light that fills the room and drives away every shadow.

"My love," she breathes. "You waited."

"Forever," he replies. "I would have waited forever."

The chains binding Eliza shatter into a thousand motes of silver light that float upward like fireflies ascending to heaven. But she doesn't attack. She simply stands there, holding Thomas's hand, looking into his eyes with all the love that death could not destroy.

Together, they begin to fade.

"Peace," Eliza whispers, looking back at you. "I can finally find peace. Tell them... tell the people of Hollow's End... I forgive them. Life is too short, and death too long, for hatred."

And then they're gone.

The manor shudders and groans. The walls begin to crumble—the entire structure was being held together by the Widow's rage. Now that she's at peace, the building is finally succumbing to its 242 years of abandonment.   
You run through collapsing corridors, down crumbling stairs, across floors that fall away into darkness. You burst through the front doors just as the entire structure implodes behind you, collapsing into rubble and dust.

You tumble down the steps and roll to a stop in the overgrown garden, gasping for breath.

And then you notice: the sky is lightening. Dawn is breaking.

The first golden rays of sunrise paint the sky in shades of pink and orange and gold. It's the most beautiful sunrise you've ever seen, made more beautiful by the simple fact that you're alive to see it.

Down in the cemetery, you watch the undead collapsing. Zombies fall back into their graves. Ghouls dissolve to dust. Skeletal warriors crumble to bones. The curse has been lifted.

After 242 years, Hollow's End is finally free.

THE AFTERMATH:

You make your way back to the village square on trembling legs. Doors begin to open. People emerge into the morning light, blinking like prisoners released from dark cells.

They see you—covered in dust and blood, holding a silver key that still glows faintly—and they understand. The curse has been broken.

A cheer erupts from the crowd. Children run into the streets for the first time in weeks. Adults embrace each other, weeping with relief. An old woman falls to her knees in prayer.

Mayor Aldric Hollow rushes from his house, his daughter Lydia at his side (safe, if you rescued her). Both are weeping openly.

"You did it!" the Mayor cries. "The curse that has haunted my family for five generations is finally broken! The sin has been forgiven! Hollow's End is FREE!"

The entire village celebrates with a feast that lasts all day. As guest of honor, you're seated at the head of the table. YOU RECEIVE:

500 Gold Pieces from the village treasury

+1 LONGSWORD OF THE HOLLOW GUARD (if you don't already have a magical weapon)

CLOAK OF PROTECTION (if you don't already have it)

POTION OF GREATER HEALING (restores all STAMINA)

The eternal gratitude of everyone in Hollow's End

"You will always have a home here," Aldric says, raising his glass. "Free food, free lodging, free drinks, for as long as you live. You saved us. You saved my daughter. You ended the curse that has haunted my family since before my grandfather's grandfather was born. We can never repay this debt, but we will spend the rest of our lives trying."

As evening approaches and you prepare to depart, you take a moment to reflect:

You faced undead horrors that would have broken lesser warriors. You navigated deadly catacombs filled with traps and monsters. You battled cultists who served darkness. You pieced together a mystery spanning 242 years. You defeated a malevolent spirit that had grown so powerful she could raise armies of the dead.

But most importantly, you brought peace to a wronged soul and forgiveness to a cursed family.

The darkness has been vanquished. The Widow has found rest with her beloved. The innocent people of Hollow's End can finally live without fear.

You shoulder your pack, now heavier with treasure and magical items, and set off toward new adventures. Behind you, villagers wave and cheer, calling blessings upon the hero who saved them.

YOUR ADVENTURE IS COMPLETE!

YOU HAVE ACHIEVED TOTAL VICTORY!

Thank you for experiencing THE CURSE OF HOLLOW'S END!

The choices you made, the battles you fought, and the mysteries you unraveled created a unique story that only you can tell. Whether this was your first attempt or your tenth, you experienced an adventure that tested your courage, challenged your mind, and hopefully entertained you.

You've achieved a temporary victory at best. The Widow will return, perhaps stronger than before.

INCOMPLETE VICTORY

You've driven back the Widow temporarily, but without the Silver Key and her true name, you couldn't bind her spirit permanently. The curse will return, perhaps within days, certainly within weeks.

Hollow's End remains doomed to eventual destruction.

sections.title: Your Adventure Ends
sections.text:
Your strength fails, and the darkness of Hollow's End closes around you. The last thing you hear is the Widow's laughter, cold and patient, echoing through the halls as your lantern gutters out.

Lydia will not be saved, and the curse of Hollow's End will claim another generation. Your adventure ends here.
